classification.difficultyReason: Students introduce auxiliary parallels at two bends, transfer angles, and decide where subtraction and addition apply. Part b repeats the numerical structure symbolically, providing scaffolding for the general expression.

spec.description: Two horizontal parallel lines joined by a three-segment zigzag; separate labels identify the top 20°, left alpha, right 50° and bottom 30° angle regions. Ordinary source-blue strokes are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The top and bottom lines are parallel. Their endpoint angles are 20° and 30°; the right interior angle is 50°.

answer.short:
$\alpha=40^\circ$.

Use horizontal auxiliary parallels to transfer the given angles.
answer.worked:
Draw horizontal lines through both interior vertices, parallel to the two given lines. At the right vertex, the lower segment makes $30^\circ$ with the horizontal by alternate angles. The middle segment therefore makes $50^\circ-30^\circ=20^\circ$ with the horizontal. Transfer this angle to the left vertex. Its upper segment also makes $20^\circ$ with the horizontal by alternate angles.

$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=20^\circ+(50^\circ-30^\circ)\\\alpha&=40^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Separate symbolic version of the parallel-horizontal-line zigzag. Gamma labels the top endpoint, x the left interior vertex, beta the right interior vertex, and alpha the bottom endpoint.
spec.mathematics: The horizontal lines are parallel; x is expressed using the three labelled angles.
spec.answerVisibility: Only symbolic givens and the unknown x are visible.

answer.short:
$x=\gamma+\beta-\alpha$.

Construct auxiliary parallels and combine alternate angles.
answer.worked:
Draw horizontal lines through both interior vertices, parallel to the given lines. At the right vertex, the lower segment makes angle $\alpha$ with the horizontal by alternate angles. The middle segment therefore makes angle $\beta-\alpha$ with the horizontal. At the left vertex, alternate angles give $\gamma$ above the horizontal and $\beta-\alpha$ below it.

$$\begin{align*}x&=\gamma+(\beta-\alpha)\\x&=\gamma+\beta-\alpha\end{align*}$$
